plan.title: Directive Version-Drift Checks and Maintenance Process

narratives.Description: Turn the initial source-baseline discipline into a repeatable maintenance workflow for released Directive updates. The process must detect stale commands and claims without making this curriculum the authority for upstream behavior.
narratives.Acceptance: A named maintainer can identify the pinned package, tag, and commit; compare a candidate upgrade with official release-matched sources and the live command surface; rerun platform-sensitive examples and literal course commands; record disagreements and required edits; update verification dates; and block publication of stale guidance until revalidation is complete.
narratives.QualityGate: Run task deft:check separately as the aggregate merge chokepoint after the literal acceptance command; do not embed the aggregate gate in plan.acceptance.commands.

items.title: Define the release-change review and claim-revalidation workflow

narrative.Acceptance: The workflow identifies authoritative inputs, changed command surfaces, claim owners, verification evidence, drift disposition, and an explicit completion gate for a new training baseline.
Focused checks catch stale pinned versions, missing traceability, and unverified taught commands without introducing a large bespoke validation framework.
